stem: A client reviews the medical record and says, ‘This allergy entry is wrong. Please delete it from my chart right now.’ Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Explain that the client has the right to request an amendment or correction through the covered entity's process and help route the request appropriately rather than independently deleting the existing record
options.B: Delete the entry immediately and remove any trace of the original documentation because HIPAA requires records to be rewritten when a client disagrees
options.C: Tell the client that HIPAA gives no right to request correction of inaccurate or incomplete health information
options.D: Advise the client to wait until a lawsuit is filed because medical-record corrections can be requested only during legal proceedings

rationale: The HIPAA Privacy Rule gives individuals the right to request amendment of protected health information in a designated record set. A covered entity must have a process to receive and act on the request; it may grant or deny the amendment under specified conditions and, if denied, the individual may submit a statement of disagreement. The bedside nurse should facilitate the formal process rather than erase or rewrite the existing record outside authorized documentation procedures.
educational_objective: Protect client rights by recognizing the HIPAA right to request amendment of inaccurate or incomplete health information and using the formal record-correction process.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — Office for Civil Rights
source_document_title: Your Medical Records; 45 CFR §164.526 Amendment of Protected Health Information

source_claim_supported: HIPAA gives individuals a federal right to request amendment of designated-record-set PHI; amendment follows a formal covered-entity process rather than ad hoc deletion.

audit_findings.source_audit: HHS/OCR patient-rights guidance and 45 CFR 164.526 verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Right to request amendment, covered-entity response process and potential denial/disagreement pathway are federally supported.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; HIPAA does not require bedside deletion/erasure of original records.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; amendment is an explicit HIPAA right.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; request is not contingent on litigation.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A respects both the client's federal right and controlled documentation process.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are responses to the correction request.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked state-law record-retention variation, amendment-versus-access distinction, denial grounds and nurse authority; federal construct remains nationally applicable.
